newsitem.title: MONACO: SOCCER-MONACO WARY OF ASPRILLA FACTOR.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-MONACO WARY OF ASPRILLA FACTOR.

text.p: Monaco look set to slip into a counter-attacking role which should suit them when they defend a 1-0 first-leg lead in their UEFA Cup quarter-final home leg against England's Newcastle United on Tuesday.

But they will be acutely aware of the threat posed by in-form Colombian Faustino Asprilla, suspended for the first leg, who scored twice when Newcastle beat another French side, Metz, in the previous round.
"Asprilla is coming back, he's fantastic and will be an extra danger," France defender Patrick Blondeau said. "Let's be calm and avoid going out to try to overrun them."

Newcastle, their attack depleted by injury to England strike pair Alan Shearer and Les Ferdinand, are obliged to take the game to Monaco as they look to recover the ground lost at St James' Park two weeks ago.

Monaco have an extremely solid defence -- only two goals against in their last five matches -- which soaked up Newcastle pressure with relative ease in England while Brazilian Anderson and teenager Thierry Henry were a constant threat with their speed on the break.

But Newcastle's seven goals in their last two games have not gone unnoticed in the principality -- including the combination between Asprilla and Frenchman David Ginola for a spectacular strike at Liverpool a week ago.
Coach Jean Tigana said: "I fear their mental (spirit), I saw them against Liverpool.

"The start of the match will be decisive, we must not get it wrong... In any case it will be a different match from the first (leg). Asprilla's going to play, they'll be organised differently...We know they can score against anyone."

Tigana will be hoping Anderson, who has scored four goals in the competition, can find the net again as he did in Newcastle and that his team can draw inspiration from a rare capacity crowd at the Louis II stadium.
Asprilla, who helped Italy's Parma win the European Cup Winners' Cup in 1993 and the UEFA Cup in 1995, has scored five goals in five UEFA Cup matches this season.
Monaco will probably tighten their ball-winning section with Emmanuel Petit, who missed the first leg through injury, playing instead of Scotland's John Collins in midfield.
Newcastle should field the Asprilla-inspired side which beat Coventry 4-0 at home at the weekend.
Monaco - Fabien Barthez; Lilian Martin, Franck Dumas, Martin Djetou, Patrick Blondeau; Emmanuel Petit, Gilles Grimandi, Sylvain Legwinski, Ali Benarbia; Sonny Anderson, Thierry Henry.
Newcastle - Shaka Hislop; Steve Watson, Darren Peacock, Philippe Albert, Robbie Elliot; Warren Barton, David Batty, Robert Lee, David Ginola; Peter Beardsley, Faustino Asprilla.
